refutation_attempt: Disassembled XNA 4.0 Game.Tick and GameClock (monodis) to test the claimed XNA contract: per-tick elapsed is clamped to 500 ms and Tick returns at a zero step count before AdvanceFrameTime and before storing the accumulator, so XNA does not update above about 508 ms either.
reason: CNA behaviour is real (clamp, then compare), but the stated XNA contract is false: XNA 4.0 has the same ceiling (500 ms plus a 1/64 snap window, about 508 ms) and neither updates nor draws above it. An inherited limitation of an accepted-but-unsupported target, not a divergence; only CNA's extra 2 Hz draws differ.

correction.title: A fixed-step TargetElapsedTime above 500 ms never produces an Update from Game::Tick, essentially the same ceiling XNA 4.0 has
correction.summary: With IsFixedTimeStep true, Game::Tick clamps the accumulator to MaxElapsedTime (500 ms) before its update loop, so a TargetElapsedTime above 500 ms is never reached: Update does not run while Draw keeps running about twice a second. XNA 4.0's Tick has essentially the same ceiling (about 508 ms, because of its 1/64 snap), so the limit is inherited; the setter accepts such a value silently.
correction.expected: Microsoft's documentation says a fixed-step Game tries to call Update on the interval in TargetElapsedTime, and the setter rejects only zero and negative values (as CNA's does), so a one-second target might be expected to update once a second. Neither XNA 4.0 nor CNA delivers that: the effective contract is a target of at most about 500 ms. CNA's Game.hpp documents only 'positive and non-zero'.
correction.actual: Game::Tick waits until accumulatedElapsedTime_ reaches TargetElapsedTime_, polls events, then clamps the accumulator to MaxElapsedTime (500 ms); the update loop 'while accumulated >= TargetElapsedTime_' therefore never runs for a target above 500 ms, stepCount stays zero, and the tick still draws, about twice a second. XNA 4.0 (IL of Game.Tick and GameClock) clamps the per-tick elapsed time to 500 ms, snaps an elapsed value within 1/64 of the target to the target, divides the sum with its leftover accumulator by the target and, when the quotient is zero, returns before GameClock.AdvanceFrameTime and before storing the sum, so its accumulator never reaches a target above about 508 ms and it neither updates nor draws. The difference is that CNA keeps drawing and that a target between 500 and 508 ms works in XNA only.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading Game::Tick at 009d40f5 and the disassembled IL of XNA 4.0's Game.Tick and GameClock (xna4-decomp dlls); the earlier claim that XNA accumulates across ticks and updates once per second is not supported by that IL. Not executed.

refutation_attempt: Searched all modules, the C API and platform layers for any reader of InactiveSleepTime or IsActive_ (a compensating sleep in Tick, RunLoop, PollEvents or the platform Delay path) and compared with XNA's Tick IL, which sleeps when not active. Only the accessors reference it.
reason: InactiveSleepTime_ is stored, validated and returned but never read; Game.hpp and runtime.h document it as the inactive-loop sleep and XNA's Tick sleeps on it. Class and low severity hold; the smoke test cited only round-trips the value.

refutation_attempt: Disassembled XNA Game.Tick and GameClock and modelled a fixed-step tick after a 2 s Update plus ResetElapsedTime: the forced-zero tick returns at a zero step count before AdvanceFrameTime, so the next tick re-measures the load, clamps to 500 ms, runs about 30 catch-up updates.
reason: The premise that XNA yields no catch-up burst in fixed-step mode is false: XNA's burst is only one tick later (about 30 updates against CNA's 29), and Game.hpp documents the flag as 'for the next variable-timestep update'. The only residue, XNA also clearing its running-slowly counters, is too small for a medium bug.

refutation_attempt: Compared CNA's updateFrameLag_ rule with XNA's Tick IL (updatesSinceRunningSlowly1/2, below 20, assigned before every Update) and hand-simulated a lone hitch, two hitches 15 ticks apart, and one large hitch: results differ as claimed. No CNA text claims the FNA rule is intended.
reason: The divergence follows from the IL: XNA flags on a second multi-step tick within 20 ticks and assigns before each Update; CNA uses FNA's lag counter and assigns after the updates. GameTimeTests covers property storage only, so no test touches the slow-frame rule.

refutation_attempt: Re-derived XNA's two zero updates from IL: RunGame's initial Update passes ElapsedGameTime zero and GameClock's first UpdateElapsedTime yields zero; then read CNA's variable branch and Run()'s counter seeding, which give the first Update microseconds and the second a full interval.
reason: Both the recorded XNA values and the IL agree; CNA's variable branch lacks the fixed branch's zero-first-update rule. Nit: the first Update sees only the microseconds since Run() seeded the counter (not initialisation time), the second a whole frame interval.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a build guard, opt-out or documented feature status for F9/F10 (docs, plans, headers) and re-read every renderer override plus EasyGL's texture recreate path. The unconditional handler stands; the DXT 'come back blank' claim is false because recreate reads the retained compressed blocks.
reason: Unconditional debug hotkeys are real and contradict XNA (no reserved keys) and CNA's own 'test-only' comments; medium fits (D3D11/12 stop drawing, WebGPU throws). But EasyGL re-uploads DXT data from compressedLevels_, so the DXT-blank effect and the reproduction built on it are wrong.

correction.actual:
After passing each event to PlatformInputBridge::ProcessEvent, Game::PollEvents calls GraphicsDevice_.GetRenderer().DebugSimulateContextLoss() for a pressed, non-repeated KeyCode::F9 and DebugRestoreContext() for F10, unconditionally (no build, option or opt-out guard). The game still sees the key, and the framework action happens as well. What the press does depends on the renderer (read at 009d40f5):
EasyGL on the desktop: F9 and F10 both print a line to std::cerr, notify MetaGL of a context loss, recreate the native context through the platform, reload the GL entry points and recreate every registered resource. EasyGLTextureRenderer::recreate_gl_resource re-uploads level 0 from the CPU shadow; DXT1/DXT3/DXT5 textures are re-uploaded from their retained compressed blocks (UploadLevel falls back to compressedLevels_ when it is given no pixels); a texture with no surviving shadow (context recovery disabled) is re-created as zeros.
DirectX 9, 11 and 12: F9 marks the device lost and reports RendererDeviceEvent::Lost; the DirectX 11 and 12 renderers then refuse CanBeginDrawEXT(), so the game stops drawing until F10 performs the reset.
Direct2D: F9 recreates the complete device-resource domain.
WebGPU: F9 throws System::NotSupportedException while a TextureCube, RenderTargetCube, Texture3D, occlusion query or custom ShaderEffect is alive; nothing in PollEvents, Tick or Run catches it, so natively it ends Run() and in the browser loop it is logged and the loop stops.
GDI overrides both hooks with empty bodies; the remaining renderers use the no-op defaults.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (PollEvents) and every override of the two hooks at 009d40f5 (EasyGL, DirectX 9/11/12, Direct2D, WebGPU, GDI). The earlier statement that DXT textures come back blank on EasyGL is withdrawn: UploadLevel takes the retained compressed blocks from compressedLevels_ when recreate_gl_resource passes no pixels, so the reproduction's 'DXT texture is re-created without data' does not occur; the visible EasyGL effect is the two stderr lines and a full context recreation. The golden transcript records a debug-hotkey-f9 scenario, so the handler is known and pinned as observable behaviour; nothing documents it as a user-facing feature. Not executed.

refutation_attempt: Read both loop bodies for compensation (IsFixedTimeStep, suppressDraw_ or forceElapsedTimeToZero_ reads on the browser path, exception handling in RunLoop/Run) and searched CNA docs for an intended browser clock. None found; the doc covers only lifetime. The C API's JS-driven route uses RunOneFrame instead.
reason: Every listed divergence holds in the Emscripten callback: fixed steps regardless of IsFixedTimeStep, full first step, TotalGameTime advanced before Update, no suppressDraw_/forceElapsedTimeToZero_, exceptions swallowed into a normal Run() return. Scope note: only Game::Run() callers; the JS-driven C API wasm route calls RunOneFrame (native Tick).

refutation_attempt: Looked for anything that clears the stored Game pointer or drops the subscriptions when a Game dies (Game::Dispose(bool), ~Game, a Disposed subscription, use of the service inside runtime) and for the static outliving main's locals. Nothing compensates; EventHandler::Remove erases without a liveness check.
reason: A function-local static service keeps a raw Game*; a stack Game dies before static destruction, so ~PhoneApplicationService::DetachEXT calls Remove on dead events (undefined behaviour at exit). The header only promises safety when the service dies first. Medium is generous for an exit-time fault in the optional phone module.

refutation_attempt: Read XNA GameComponent.Dispose(bool) IL/decompile (removes from Game.Components, then raises Disposed) against CNA's version, and searched CNA for compensation: a Game subscription to component Disposed, C API disposal route, header text documenting the difference. None exists; the tests never call Dispose on a component.
reason: XNA's removal is confirmed (IL only; the XNA docs are silent) and CNA's Dispose(true) only raises Disposed, so a 'disposed' component stays registered and keeps updating/drawing. Undocumented in CNA; possible C++ reason (shared-owned collection could destroy the component mid-Dispose) is not recorded anywhere.

refutation_attempt: Read Game::Dispose(bool)'s loop (count re-read each pass, live Components_[i]) and XNA's Dispose IL (array copy first); traced a self-removing component at index 0 and found b skipped. Looked for a snapshot or lock elsewhere in Dispose and for tests that dispose mutating components; none.
reason: The live-index walk is exactly as described and XNA snapshots first; a Dispose override that removes itself or a peer skips the next component. Latent for CNA's own components (none remove themselves) and reachable via the natural workaround for CNA-BUG-086, hence low. Distinct root from BUG-086.

refutation_attempt: Grepped every write to Game's cached graphicsDeviceService_/graphicsDeviceManager_ (only constructor and first resolution), re-read registerServices/unregisterServices/Dispose(bool), and checked the idiomatic member-of-derived-game order by hand: it is safe. Non-nested lifetimes dangle exactly as claimed; the C API comment concurs.
reason: All three one-way references exist: an untracked ClientSizeChanged lambda, cached raw pointers in Game never cleared, and ~GraphicsDeviceManager dereferencing game_. Only non-nested lifetimes are affected (the idiomatic shape is safe), so low severity stands; the C API's RetiredManagers comment corroborates it.

refutation_attempt: Read XNA's GraphicsDeviceManager.Dispose(bool): it has no guard at all, so a Disposed handler that disposes again recurses identically. Checked CNA's tests and header for a re-entrancy contract: only sequential repeat disposal is pinned, and the disposed_ guard already exceeds XNA.
reason: Re-entrant Dispose from the manager's own Disposed event is not contractual: XNA has the same recursion (no guard), the header states nothing, and CNA's regression test covers sequential repeats, which the guard satisfies. Setting the flag first would be tidier, but that is a robustness nit, not a contract breach. Cited comparison is a sibling class's design choice.

refutation_attempt: Disassembled XNA's GraphicsDeviceInformation.set_Adapter (monodis) to test the cited IL: it loads the stored adapter field, not the argument, so real XNA does not reject the first null. Re-read applyToExistingRenderer and both GraphicsDevice::Reset overloads: the null dereference and silent 'keep adapter' fallback are as described.
reason: The XNA IL claim is wrong (the check tests the field), though the XNA docs still list ArgumentNullException; CNA's setter accepts null. The CNA-specific hazard stands: applyToExistingRenderer forms a reference from a null pointer although ApplyChanges/CreateDevice already guard null when naming the device. Low severity holds.

correction.summary: XNA's documentation says the GraphicsDeviceInformation.Adapter setter throws ArgumentNullException for a null value (the shipped IL only tests the stored adapter, so the first null slips through in real XNA). CNA's setter stores any pointer, and applyToExistingRenderer then passes *gdi.getAdapterProperty() to GraphicsDevice::Reset, which is undefined behaviour for a null adapter; in practice the device keeps its previous adapter.
correction.expected: The XNA 4.0 documentation for GraphicsDeviceInformation.Adapter lists ArgumentNullException ("Adapter is null. Try using DefaultAdapter instead."), so a PreparingDeviceSettings handler is told not to produce a device information without an adapter. (The IL of set_Adapter tests the stored field rather than the incoming value, so real XNA 4.0 lets the first null through and fails later; the documented contract is the exception.) Independently of XNA, CNA's own code must not form a reference through a null pointer.
correction.actual: modules/runtime/src/GraphicsDeviceInformation.cpp stores any pointer in setAdapterProperty. ApplyChanges and CreateDevice in modules/runtime/src/GraphicsDeviceManager.cpp already guard the adapter with a null check when they name the device, but applyToExistingRenderer then calls graphicsDevice_->Reset(pp, *gdi.getAdapterProperty()), forming a reference from a null pointer, which is undefined behaviour. With current compilers the address simply reaches the pointer overload of GraphicsDevice::Reset, which treats null as "keep the current adapter", so the handler's mistake is silently ignored rather than reported.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5 and disassembling XNA 4.0's GraphicsDeviceInformation.set_Adapter, which loads the adapter field instead of the argument; the earlier statement that the IL rejects a null value is withdrawn, while the XNA documentation still lists the exception. Not executed; the practical outcome depends on the compiler not exploiting the undefined behaviour.

refutation_attempt: Searched every rebind site (setWindowInternal is called only in Game's constructor), the window rebuild paths (resolveRenderer runs only from the device constructor) and member destruction order (Window_ dies before GraphicsDevice_ with a trivial dtor). Only an explicit device Dispose() leaves GameWindow::window_ dangling, as claimed.
reason: GraphicsDevice::Dispose resets the owning platformWindow_, and GameWindow keeps a raw pointer that nothing clears, so later Window calls (SetTitle, GetClientBounds, native handle) hit freed memory. XNA's window survives device disposal. Narrow trigger (explicit disposal of the Game's device), so low severity is fair.

refutation_attempt: Checked each declaration's access section and marker, XNA 4.0's decompiled Texture and GameWindow for the six names (absent), CHECKLIST.md and CNAHelper.hpp for the rule, plans/docs for a deliberate omission (only an EXT-suffix convention note) and the strict tests' coverage (Devices only).
reason: All six public non-XNA members are unmarked while neighbours carry CNAEXT, and the CNA-repo checklist and macro comment require the marker, so a strict build passes them silently. An older EXT-name-suffix convention exists but is not what the checklist asks. Same defect class as CNA-BUG-075 but different members, so not a duplicate.

refutation_attempt: Traced the namespace-scope initialiser -> PublishAvailable -> RebuildAttemptOrder -> GetSelected -> ConsultEnvironmentOnce and both throw sites (unknown name, RejectIfNotCompiledIn with fallback off); looked for a catch, a deferred/lazy read, or a doc saying the failure is process-fatal. None; docs only say it 'throws'.
reason: Both throws escape the initialisation of a non-local static, which the language turns into std::terminate before main, contradicting the source comment and runtime-renderer-selection.md ('throws', publish before main). Still a loud, diagnosable failure on an unusual input, so low severity stands.

refutation_attempt: Re-read every public *Exception header base (grep of modules/*/include), the ContentLoadException rationale comment, both cited tests, the C API barrier arms and Sharp Runtime's Exception base (next 41b918c9); looked for a CNA doc promising a System::Exception base. All statements hold; the divergence is documented in-header.
reason: ContentLoadException and PlatformException derive from std::runtime_error, XNA-named graphics, audio, gamer, net, devices and pipeline exceptions from System::Exception, and the header states the choice is deliberate and pinned by tests. Documented narrowing, so a gap rather than a bug is right.

refutation_attempt: Read Logger.cpp end to end and Logger.hpp for any thread-safety or re-entrancy statement, an atomic level, a recursive mutex, or a call outside the lock. minimumLevel_ is a plain static read unlocked; the sink runs under a non-recursive std::mutex that SetSink/ResetSink also take.
reason: Both limits follow directly from the storage and locking, and neither is documented; concurrent Log calls themselves are safe. Nothing promises otherwise, so a limitation/gap (undocumented precondition) fits better than a bug. No test is concurrent or re-entrant.

refutation_attempt: Searched the tree for any definition of CNA::Runtime members and any include of CNA/Misc.hpp (none), then read the guard: it is the CApi_UnimplementedRuntimeFacade CTest test in the C API sub-build, not a build failure, and exists only when CNA_BUILD_C_API is ON (default OFF).
reason: The facade really is declared, documented as working, and defined nowhere. The text's 'fails the build' is inaccurate: the guard is a CTest test that only exists in the opt-in C API build, so the record is guarded only where that test runs.

correction.actual: CNA/Misc.hpp declares RuntimeOptions (four flags) and Runtime with five methods and Doxygen describing working behaviour. No source defines them and no translation unit includes the header, so a program that calls any method fails at link time. The C API records the rows as not applicable because the facade "is declared and defined nowhere". The CApi_UnimplementedRuntimeFacade CTest test (CheckUnimplementedRuntimeFacade.cmake, which runs nm over the runtime archive) fails the day CNA::Runtime:: symbols appear, so the gap is known and guarded; that test is defined only in builds configured with CNA_BUILD_C_API, which is off by default, and it fails a test run rather than the build. The header itself does not say the facade is unimplemented. Game is the working startup boundary.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading modules/runtime/include/CNA/Misc.hpp, modules/c-api/cmake/CheckUnimplementedRuntimeFacade.cmake, its add_test registration in modules/c-api/CMakeLists.txt and the coverage mapping at 009d40f5, and by searching the tree for includes of the header and for definitions of the methods (none). CNA's own check inspects the compiled runtime archive with nm; it was not run here.

refutation_attempt: Grepped the tree for other references to the hook (none), read Game::Run's catch blocks and XNA's RunGame (both requirement exceptions offered to the hook, rethrow only on false), then traced where CNA throws them: graphics ones come from the device constructor inside Game's constructor.
reason: The hook is declared, XNA calls it, CNA never does; class stands. But the graphics exception is thrown from Game's constructor rather than Run, so 'the exception escapes Run' and the proposed Run-level test only fit exceptions raised during Run, such as audio.

correction.actual: CNA's implementation returns false and is referenced nowhere else: Game::Run in modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp logs any escaping exception and rethrows it without consulting the hook, so an override is never called. Only exceptions raised inside Run can reach that handler (for example NoAudioHardwareException from SoundEffect or DynamicSoundEffectInstance during LoadContent). The NoSuitableGraphicsDeviceException throw sites read at 009d40f5 (the UseNullDevice/UseReferenceDevice renderer requirement and the DirectX 9 HiDef shader-model check) run while a GraphicsDevice is constructed, which for Game's own device happens in Game's constructor, before Run exists; a hook wired into Run alone would not see those.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5 and searching the tree for other references to the hook (none). XNA call site read from the decompiled XNA 4.0 Game.RunGame. Not executed; where each CNA exception is thrown was established by reading, so a regression test has to raise the exception during Run (for example from LoadContent) to reach a wired hook.

refutation_attempt: Grepped every LoadContent/UnloadContent call site in runtime: DrawableGameComponent calls LoadContent once in Initialize and UnloadContent only in Dispose; OnDeviceCreated is never subscribed; Game and the manager do not forward device events to components. Compared XNA's Initialize/Dispose decompile: it subscribes four service events.
reason: XNA's DrawableGameComponent requires the service and follows DeviceCreated/DeviceDisposing; CNA's component does neither and its source comment ('Until that service exists') is stale since the manager registers the service. Real but narrow, because Game rarely re-creates its device; a gap fits. The cited tests never call Initialize.

refutation_attempt: Grepped the whole tree for FindBestDevice, RankDevices and CanResetDevice: only the definitions and header declarations exist. Read CreateDevice/ApplyChanges (direct GraphicsDeviceInformation construction, in-place Reset) and XNA's ChangeDevice decompile, which calls FindBestDevice then CanResetDevice.
reason: The three virtuals are never invoked by CNA, so overrides are silently ignored, while XNA's ChangeDevice consults them. The headers document what each returns when called, not that CNA calls them, and CNA has a single adapter, so a gap rather than a bug is defensible.

refutation_attempt: Recounted: 99 CNA headers include Prop.hpp (9) or SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp (90), Prop.hpp defines 31 macros, Helper adds CONTAINS and INTERNAL (33), no #undef anywhere. Checked that Helper does not pull in Prop.hpp (it does not) and that Game.hpp reaches Prop.hpp through ContentManager.hpp.
reason: All counts and macro names verified at sharp-runtime next 41b918c9 (Prop.hpp unchanged since 2026-07-25). Nuance: only 9 headers include Prop.hpp directly and the other 90 leak just CONTAINS and INTERNAL, but Game.hpp reaches Prop.hpp transitively, so every game TU sees all 33. No CNA text promises macro hygiene.
